title: ESSAY 11: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code — Transforming India's Credit Culture

blocks.content: (Word Count: ~300 words | Type: Analytical | Level: SBI PO / RBI / CBO / IBPS SO)

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016 consolidated existing fragmented insolvency laws into a single unified statutory framework.
It fundamentally shifted India's credit ecosystem from a 'debtor-in-possession' model to a 'creditor-in-control' framework.
The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) operates as the statutory regulator overseeing insolvency professionals, agencies, and information utilities.
The framework prioritizes business reorganization and asset value maximization over premature liquidation.

blocks.content: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code marks a paradigm shift from a debtor-in-possession model to a creditor-in-control framework, reshaping India's credit culture.

Before the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) came into force in December 2016, India's insolvency framework was a labyrinthine patchwork of overlapping legislations — the SICA (Sick Industrial Companies Act), the Companies Act provisions, the SARFAESI Act, and the RDDBFI Act — that allowed defaulting promoters to retain control of their companies for decades, frustrating creditors and misallocating economic resources. The World Bank's Doing Business Report ranked India 136th out of 189 countries for resolving insolvency in 2015, with a typical insolvency process taking 4.3 years and recovering only 25.7 cents on the dollar.

rows: Creditor-in-control (Committee of Creditors takes over management)
Time-bound (target 180 days, extendable up to 330 days)
Business reorganization and asset value preservation

blocks.content: The IBC represented a paradigm shift: from a debtor-in-possession to a creditor-in-control regime. Upon admission of an insolvency application by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), a moratorium immediately freezes all legal proceedings against the corporate debtor. A Resolution Professional takes over management from the promoters. The Committee of Creditors (CoC), comprising all financial creditors whose claims have been verified, exercises sovereign judgment over the resolution plan — a commercial decision that courts are instructed not to second-guess (as affirmed by the Supreme Court in the Essar Steel case, 2019). If no resolution plan is approved within the stipulated 330 days, the company proceeds to liquidation with a defined waterfall mechanism for distributing proceeds.

The outcomes have been transformative. By March 2024, over Rs. 3.16 lakh crore in creditor claims had been resolved under IBC — with banks recovering significantly higher amounts than they would have through conventional processes. Landmark resolutions — Essar Steel acquired by ArcelorMittal, Bhushan Steel by Tata Steel, Jaypee Infratech by Suraksha Group — demonstrated that even India's largest distressed assets could be revived in new hands. The 'IBC fear factor' has demonstrably improved promoter behaviour, with defaults increasingly being settled before formal insolvency proceedings are initiated.

items: NCLT acts as the Adjudicating Authority for Corporate Insolvency (CIRP), whereas DRT handles Individuals and Partnership Firms.
The maximum outer time limit for completing the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) is 330 days, including legal proceedings.
Section 53 of the IBC mandates the 'Waterfall Mechanism' detailing the exact priority order for asset distribution during liquidation.

blocks.content: Challenges remain — NCLT capacity constraints, the treatment of home buyers as financial creditors, the treatment of operational creditors, and the need for pre-packaged resolution mechanisms for MSMEs. But the IBC has fundamentally and irreversibly changed India's credit culture: the message to borrowers is now clear — default has consequences.

Examiner's Tip: IBC essays must mention the Essar Steel Supreme Court case, Rs.3.16 lakh crore resolution, the 330-day limit, and the shift from debtor-in-possession to creditor-in-control. These details signal comprehensive preparation.
